class.name: NetwSessionCore
class.brief_description: The session lifecycle machine: what state a session is in, what role the local peer plays in it, and which inbound joins are worth looking at.
class.description: The machine holds no [Object] and sends nothing, which is what lets a session with no scene tree, no node and no connect verb still answer [member state] and [member role]. Opening a connection is nobody's business here and neither is authenticating one, so the peer is never reached: the interface above observes it and hands down the facts [method on_peer_assigned] needs. Every path in and out converges on [method transition], so setup and teardown stay paired. A server that vanishes reuses the graceful leave's route rather than taking an edge of its own, which is why there is no direct [constant STATE_ONLINE] to [constant STATE_OFFLINE] edge and why [method edge_is_legal] is public: the refusal is a contract a caller can check. [codeblock] OFFLINE ─assign peer─▶ CONNECTING ─success─▶ ONLINE ▲ │ │ └─── null / offline ────┘ leave / crash ───┤ │ ▼ └──────────────────────────────────── DISCONNECTING [/codeblock] The signals fire in the one order a lifecycle listener can rely on. Leaving a state announces itself before the state moves, so [signal session_ended] never fires on a connect that failed before it was ever live, and entering announces itself after, so a listener on [signal session_entered] reads the state it is in. [codeblock] transition(ONLINE) state_changed(CONNECTING, ONLINE), session_entered transition(DISCONNECTING) session_ended, state_changed(ONLINE, DISCONNECTING) transition(ONLINE) twice nothing; the same state is not a re-entry [/codeblock]

method.name: clear
method.description: Returns the machine to [constant STATE_OFFLINE] with no role, no advertised cap, and an empty flood window. Session teardown, not an edge: nothing is announced, because there is no session left to announce it to.

method.name: compute_app_tag
method.description: Folds a build tag into the 32 bits an admission handshake carries. An empty [param value] answers zero, which disables the compatibility gate rather than matching a build named nothing. The fold is the engine's own string hash over code points, so a tag outside ASCII folds by what it spells rather than by how it is encoded.

method.name: edge_is_legal
method.description: Returns whether [method transition] admits the edge from [param from] to [param to]. Reading the table is what lets a caller route around it instead of discovering the refusal at runtime.

method.name: is_server_role
method.description: Returns whether [member role] carries server authority. Both [constant ROLE_DEDICATED_SERVER] and [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER] do, and very little should ask for one of them specifically.

method.name: join_flooded
method.description: Returns whether [param sender]'s join frames have exceeded the flood window, counting this one. An honest peer submits one join and at most two, so the budget drops a flood without touching a legitimate burst of clients arriving together. A [param sender] of 1 is the host joining itself, which carries authority and is never limited. [param now_msec] is an argument rather than a reading, which is the whole reason the window is testable: a wall clock cannot be asked to be a second past itself.

method.name: on_peer_assigned
method.description: Reacts to a peer the interface above just handed the session, which is the one edge every host, join, test rig and embedded-server path already crosses. [param has_live_peer] is [code]false[/code] for a null or offline assignment, and that is how a cancelled connect arrives rather than through an abort verb of its own. Cancelling only collapses a session that was still [constant STATE_CONNECTING]: a null assignment while live is left alone, because a deleted tree nulls the peer that way and a leave or a crash owns that teardown instead. A server peer is born live whether or not its transport says so, so a [param unique_id] of 1 reaches [constant STATE_ONLINE] here through [method resolve_online]. A client is still mid-handshake and waits.

method.name: resolve_online
method.description: Completes a connect with the role [param unique_id] and [member desired_role] imply, and enters [constant STATE_ONLINE]. Peer identity decides authority and the hint only splits it: a [param unique_id] of 1 is a server, [constant ROLE_LISTEN_SERVER] when that is what was asked for and [constant ROLE_DEDICATED_SERVER] otherwise. Anything else is a [constant ROLE_CLIENT] whatever the hint says.

method.name: transition
method.description: Advances [member state] along a legal edge, announcing the exit before the move and the entry after it. The only entry point allowed to move [member state], so every path converges on one set of transitions instead of one per caller. Moving to the state already held does nothing, which is what keeps a transport repeating its connection signal from firing a second [signal session_entered]. An edge [method edge_is_legal] refuses fails and leaves the machine where it was.

members.member: The player cap the live host advertises, or zero while this session is not hosting. Whatever opened the host stamps the cap it resolved, so a probe is answered with a plain session fact rather than with the configuration the host was built from.

The role the local peer intends to play, pushed down from the session configuration above. It is read only by [method resolve_online] and only to split a server, so a session that intends to be a client and is handed peer 1 still hosts.
The role the local peer plays in the current session, resolved by [method resolve_online] before [constant STATE_ONLINE] is entered.
The current connection state of the session. Assigning it moves the value and announces the edge, and nothing else. Drive it through [method transition] so the exit and entry hooks run.

signal.name: session_ended
signal.description: Emitted on leaving [constant STATE_ONLINE], before the state moves. Never fires on a connect that failed before it was live, which is the one guarantee that placement buys.

signal.name: session_entered
signal.description: Emitted on entering [constant STATE_ONLINE], once [member role] is resolved and the state has moved.

signal.name: state_changed
signal.description: Emitted whenever [member state] moves. The edge doubles as the notification that a peer was assigned, which [MultiplayerAPI] never surfaces on its own, so a consumer that wants to observe "a peer just changed" binds here.

constants.constant: A peer is assigned and the connection is being established. The only state a cancellation can collapse.
The session has an active [MultiplayerPeer] and a resolved [member role].
The session is closing the active peer and clearing its state. A crash passes through here rather than around it.
No session role has been assigned yet.
Connected to a remote server as a client.
Hosts the session without acting as a local client.
Hosts the session and also represents the local player.
